memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Once a year Aaron shall make atonement on its horns. This annual atonement must be made with the blood of the atoning sin offering for the generations to come. It is most holy to the Lord." - Exodus 30:10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is something humbling. Even the altar of prayer required atonement. Once a year, blood was applied to its horns, because even the place where prayers rose to God needed cleansing. The instrument of worship itself was touched by the sinfulness of the people who used it.

That should keep us honest. Our prayers are not pure. They are mixed with self-interest, distraction, half-belief, and sometimes outright selfishness. Even our worship needs covering. If we imagine our devotion is what commends us to God, this verse quietly corrects us.

But this is not cause for despair — it is cause for gratitude. We have a High Priest who intercedes for us, and the Spirit Himself helps us in our weakness, interceding when we do not know what we ought to pray (Rom 8:26-27). Your imperfect prayers are carried, cleansed, and presented by Christ. So pray anyway. Do not wait until your motives are pure, because they never will be. Bring your mixed and stumbling prayers to the God who has already provided for their cleansing.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I hold back from prayer because my motives feel impure?
How does it free me that Christ presents even my imperfect prayers to the Father?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, even my prayers need Your cleansing, yet You receive them through Christ. Thank You that I need not wait for pure motives. I bring You my stumbling prayers today. Amen.
